passage:
Thursday
Today scared me. After PE, Dhruv was sitting on the changing-room bench, gasping and shaking, saying, "I can't breathe, I can't breathe." For a second I thought something terrible was happening to his heart, and my own hands went cold. I didn't know what to do, so I did what our coach once told us. I sat next to him, not too close, and talked slowly. "I'm here. You're breathing. Try breathing out long, like me." I asked the others to wait outside so it was quieter, and sent Anu to get Coach in case he needed a doctor. By the time Coach came, Dhruv's breathing was slower. Coach stayed with him and called his parents. Tonight he texted me: "Thanks for not leaving." I'm still shaky.
Kalyani

qa.q: Where was Dhruv sitting after PE?
qa.a: Dhruv was sitting on the changing-room bench.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling when Dhruv said he couldn't breathe?
qa.a: Kalyani was frightened, fearing something terrible was happening to Dhruv's heart, and felt cold hands.

qa.q: Which of Kalyani's actions helped, and why?
qa.a: Staying near, talking slowly, clearing the room so it was quieter and sending for Coach in case a doctor was needed all kept Dhruv calmer and safer.

qa.q: What might Dhruv have felt when he texted "Thanks for not leaving"?
qa.a: Dhruv likely felt grateful and relieved that someone stayed beside him while he felt he could not breathe.

grounding: A friend sees someone gasping and shaking, fears something terrible is happening, and helps by staying near, speaking slowly, keeping it quiet and calling an adult.

passage: The local bus to the taluka school was packed, and the driver had the film songs turned up loud. Halfway there, Leela grabbed Darshan's arm. She was gasping, her hands shaking. 'I can't breathe. Something's wrong.' Darshan's stomach dropped. He had never seen her like this. He made himself speak slowly. 'I'm here. Look at me. Breathe out with me.' He asked the conductor to turn the music down and pushed the window wide. The auntie beside them gave up her seat. 'Does your chest hurt? Should we go to the health centre?' Leela shook her head. 'It's… easing.' After some minutes her breathing slowed. At school, Darshan took her straight to their class teacher, who sat with Leela, phoned her mother and asked her to take Leela for a check-up that evening.

qa.q: What did Darshan ask the conductor to do?
qa.a: Turn the music down.

qa.q: What did Darshan feel when Leela grabbed his arm?
qa.a: He was frightened and shocked, since he had never seen her like this, but he made himself speak slowly.

qa.q: Which of Darshan's actions helped most, and why?
qa.a: Staying close, speaking slowly and making the bus calmer and airier, while checking whether she needed the health centre.

qa.q: How might the episode have felt for Leela?
qa.a: It probably felt terrifying, as if she could not breathe, and having Darshan steady beside her likely made it less lonely.

grounding: Shows a friend seeing someone gasp and shake, fearing the worst, and helping by staying close, speaking slowly, calming the surroundings and getting adult and medical help.

passage: The concert in the Copenhagen park was so loud Ulla felt it in her ribs. Then she noticed Emeka wasn't singing. He was bent over, gasping, his whole body trembling. 'I can't breathe. My chest,' he said. Ulla's own heart jumped. What if it was his heart? She took his arm. 'Let's get out of the crowd. Slowly. I'm with you.' They edged to the back, by a tree. She kept her words short. 'Sit. Breathe out long. I'm here.' He was still clutching his chest, so she waved down a steward and asked for the first-aid tent. A medic checked Emeka's pulse and listened to his chest. 'Everything sounds okay. It looks like a panic attack. Stay here till it settles.' Twenty minutes later Emeka was sipping water, pale but steady. Ulla held his hand all the way home.

qa.q: Where did Ulla take Emeka first?
qa.a: To the back, by a tree.

qa.q: What was Ulla worried about when Emeka said 'My chest'?
qa.a: She was frightened that something serious might be wrong with his heart.

qa.q: Why was getting the first-aid tent a good step?
qa.a: Emeka's chest pain could have been serious, so having a medic check him was the safe choice alongside calming him.

qa.q: How might Emeka feel about Ulla staying with him?
qa.a: He is likely to feel grateful and less alone, even if embarrassed about what happened.

grounding: Shows a teenager seeing a friend gasp and tremble, fearing the worst, moving him somewhere calm, speaking simply, and getting medical help because it might be serious.

passage: In the changing room before the district volleyball final, Maria suddenly sat down on the bench, gasping and shaking. 'I can't… I can't get air.' A couple of teammates crowded round, talking at once. Hansa felt a jolt of fear. Then she remembered what the coach had said at training camp. She knelt in front of Maria and said to the others, 'Give her some space, please.' They stepped back. Hansa spoke slowly. 'You're safe. I'm staying. Feel the bench under you.' Maria's eyes were wide, her hands pressed to her chest. Hansa sent Riya to bring the coach. The coach came quickly, checked Maria, and sat with them both. After a few minutes the shaking slowed. Maria sat out the first set, and the coach phoned her mother to take her to the doctor afterwards.

qa.q: Which match was the team about to play?
qa.a: The district volleyball final.

qa.q: How did Hansa feel when Maria began gasping?
qa.a: She felt a jolt of fear, then steadied herself by remembering the coach's advice.

qa.q: What did Hansa do that a friend could copy?
qa.a: She cleared the crowd, stayed close, spoke slowly and simply, and sent for the coach.

qa.q: How might the crowding teammates have affected Maria?
qa.a: Several people talking at once probably made her feel more trapped and panicky.

grounding: Shows a teenager watching a teammate gasp and shake, and helping by staying near, speaking slowly, calming the space and fetching an adult for a medical check.

passage:
Dear Rafiq,
I keep thinking about Friday at the bus stand. When you started gasping and shaking and saying you couldn't breathe, I honestly thought something terrible was happening. My own hands were shaking. But I remembered what the school nurse once told us: stay close, talk slowly, keep things calm. So I sat next to you, moved your bag away, asked the chaiwala to turn his radio down, and kept saying, 'I'm right here. Breathe out slowly.' I also told myself that if your lips went blue or you fainted, I'd call an ambulance straight away. You came back after about ten minutes. Please tell your parents and see a doctor to be sure. You don't have to be embarrassed with me. Ever.
Chetan

qa.q: What did Chetan ask the chaiwala to do?
qa.a: Turn his radio down.

qa.q: How did Chetan feel when Rafiq started gasping?
qa.a: Chetan felt frightened that something terrible was happening, with shaking hands.

qa.q: What did Chetan do that helped?
qa.a: Stayed close, spoke slowly, calmed the surroundings, planned to call an ambulance if it looked serious, and urged Rafiq to tell the parents and see a doctor.

qa.q: How might Rafiq feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Rafiq may feel embarrassed at first, then relieved and less alone, knowing Chetan isn't judging.

grounding: A friend sees someone gasping and shaking, stays near, speaks slowly, keeps things calm and urges medical help.
